full_text:
A lot has happened since the initial [2026 NFL Super Bowl 61 Odds](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/nfl-super-bowl-61-odds#/) dropped earlier this year, and [Free Agency reorganized the Super Bowl Odds](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/super-bowl-odds-post-nfl-free-agency#/). It’s time to see which teams were the biggest risers and fallers to win the Lombardi Trophy following the 2026 NFL Draft. I already broke down the draft in our [Veteran Market Watch](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/nfl-draft-market-report-veterans#/), and I broke down the initial [2026 Rookie of the Year Odds](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/nfl-rookie-of-the-year-awards#/).

The biggest off-season transactions are mostly behind us. However, we could still see players like __A.J. Brown__, __Kayvon Thibodeaux__, __Brandon Aiyuk__, __Anthony Richardson__, __Kayshon Boutte__, and __Kenny Moore__ get traded before Week 1.

There are also some quality free agents available, including __Aaron Rodgers__, __David Njoku__, __Joey Bosa__, __Jauan Jennings__, __Stefon Diggs__, __Deebo Samuel__, __Keenan Allen__, __Tyreek Hill__, __Kevin Zeitler__, __Mekhi Becton__, __David Njoku__, __Joe Bitonio__, __Taylor Decker__, __Haason Reddick__, and __Cam Robinson__.

Always shop around multiple sportsbooks before placing any NFL futures wagers. Sportsbooks will have wildly different odds and totals based on their liabilities with different futures wagers. You can maximize your chances of winning by looking around first and finding the best odds and prices. See where I think each team sits after the draft in my updated [Power Rankings](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-draft). As always, good luck with your wagers!

---------------------------------------------

Five Biggest Risers
-------------------

### __Cincinnati Bengals__

\>+2500 odds (3.85% implied odds) to +3000 odds (3.23%)

The Bengals experienced the NFL’s biggest rise in their implied odds (+.62%) to win the Super Bowl since free agency, thanks to their bold move to flip the 10th overall pick for __Dexter Lawrence__ (NYG). The Bengals allowed the fourth-highest adjusted YBC/ATT (2.48) and the most rushing YPG (147.1), but the additions of Lawrence and __Jonathan Allen__ (Min) should solidify Cincy’s interior defensive line. The trade is also a sign that the front office wants to win now after missing the postseason in three straight seasons after reaching the 2022 AFC Championship Game. Lawrence will make an immediate impact instead of waiting for a rookie defender to develop with the 10th overall pick.

### __Tampa Bay Buccaneers__

\>+4000 odds (2.44% implied odds) to +5000 odds (1.96%)

I’m a little surprised that Tampa Bay had the NFC’s biggest rise in its implied odds (+.48%) to win the Super Bowl since the end of March, since the Saints and Panthers also saw their odds improve (check out below). The Buccaneers needed to improve their defense after __Todd Bowles__’ unit sank to 20th PPG allowed (24.2) and 19th in YPG allowed (337.2). They did just that by landing a slipping __Rueben Bain__ at No. 15, whom Brett Whitefield [called](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/dl#/) the “premier power rusher” in this class. The Buccaneers ranked 18th with 37 sacks last season, despite blitzing at the third-highest rate (35.3%). They also landed __Josiah Trotter__ in the second round, who will team up with __Alex Anzalone__ to fill the void left behind by the retired __Lavonte David__.

### __Dallas Cowboys__

\>+3000 odds (3.23% implied odds) to +3500 odds (2.78%)

America’s team started to get some love in the betting markets after the draft. The Cowboys had the largest improvement in their implied Super Bowl odds (+.45%) after landing a pair of defenders in the first round to instantly improve a defense that ranked last in PPG allowed (30.1) and 30th in YPG allowed (377.0). Dallas sent a pair of fifth-round picks to move up one spot to No. 11 to lock up __Caleb Downs__, who won the Jim Thorpe Award as the top defensive back in college football in his final season at Ohio State. Downs will pair with __Jalen Thompson__ (Ari), whom the Cowboys signed to their largest free agent deal (three years, $33 million) since 2012. Dallas recouped a pair of fourth-round picks to slide down three spots to No. 23, where they selected __Malachi Lawrence__, who will bolster a pass rush that ranked 26th in sack rate (5.5%). They also acquired San Francisco’s leading tackler from last season, __Dee Winters__, to solidify the middle of their defense for a fifth-round pick.

### __Baltimore Ravens__

\>+1050 odds (8.7% implied odds) to +1100 odds (8.33%)

The Ravens continued to rise up the Super Bowl odds board after starting the offseason at +1400. They experienced the AFC’s [biggest rise after free agency](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/super-bowl-odds-post-nfl-free-agency#/), and they’re firmly the fourth-favorites behind the Rams, Seahawks, and Bills following the draft, with their implied odds rising by .37%. Baltimore needed to rebuild the interior of its offensive line after letting __Tyler Linderbaum__ walk in free agency, and one of the best players in the draft fell to them at No. 14. __Olaivavega Ioane__ slipped to Baltimore because he plays guard, but he’s exactly what the team needs. He moves people around in the run game, and he’ll help __Derrick Henry__ remain a force at 33 years old. Baltimore was determined to improve its pass rush even after getting cold feet on a trade for __Maxx Crosby__. They quickly signed __Trey Hendrickson__ after the Crosby trade fell through, and Hendrickson has the third-most sacks (39) since 2023. Baltimore then drafted __Zion Young__ in the second round, which should boost a pass rush that ranked 31st in sack rate (4.3%).

### __Carolina Panthers/New Orleans Saints__

\>+10000 odds (.99% implied odds) to +12500 odds (.66%)

Three-quarters of the NFC South saw the biggest rise in Super Bowl odds since free agency. The Buccaneers saw the second-largest jump in their implied odds, and the Panthers and Saints were close behind with a +.33% improvement — the Falcons continued to tumble down the board since February at +12000. The Panthers used the draft to build in the trenches, selecting __Monroe Freeling__ at No. 19 and __Lee Hunter__ at No. 49. __Ikem Ekwonu__ ruptured his patellar tendon in Carolina’s playoff loss, which has him in jeopardy of missing the entire final season of his rookie contract. The Panthers signed __Jaelen Phillips__ and __Devin Lloyd__ to level up their defense, and Hunter beefs up an interior defensive line that allowed the seventh-highest adjusted YBC/ATT (2.36). The Saints had a top-heavy receiving corps led by __Chris Olave__, who accounted for 30.9% of New Orleans’ receiving yards and 27.2% of the targets. New Orleans changed its situation by selecting __Jordan Tyson__ eighth overall, __Oscar Delp__ in the third round, and __Bryce Lance__ in the fourth round, which gives __Tyler Shough__ a full deck at receiver. The Saints surged late in the season under Shough, and bettors believe it could continue in 2026 after the Patriots came from off the pack under a second-year QB.

Five Biggest Fallers
--------------------

### __Jacksonville Jaguars__

\>+3000 odds (3.23% implied odds) to +2500 odds (3.85%)

The Jaguars were awfully quiet in free agency, and they were universally panned for their haul in the draft, so it’s no surprise they saw the biggest drop in their implied odds (-.62%) to win the Super Bowl. They added only __Chris Rodriguez__ in free agency, who wasn’t tendered as a restricted free agent by the Commanders, and they lost key contributors like __Devin Lloyd__ (Car), __Travis Etienne__ (NO), and __Greg Newsome__ (NYG). They also swapped disappointing 2024 second-round defensive tackle picks with the Falcons. Jacksonville wasn’t on the clock until 56th overall because of their trade up for cornerback __Travis Hunter__ last year, and it reached multiple rounds to select TE __Nate Boerkircher__, who totaled just 38 receptions in five college seasons. GM __James Gladstone__ totally disregarded value to select players he coveted, which will either make him look like a fool or a genius in a few years.

### __Green Bay Packers__

\>+2000 odds (4.76% implied odds) to +1800 odds (5.26%)

The Packers owned limited draft capital because of their massive swing to land __Micah Parsons__ before the start of last season. Green Bay took the NFC’s biggest tumble in implied odds (-.5%) following the draft, which isn’t helped by the uncertainty surrounding Parsons and __Tucker Kraft__ for the start of the season following ACL injuries last season. The Packers didn’t pick until 52nd overall when they selected __Brandon Cisse__ to address their biggest need at cornerback. He’ll compete with free-agent signee __Benjamin St-Juste__ for a starting job across from __Keisean Nixon__ after the Packers released __Nate Hobbs__ just one year in a four-year, $48 million deal. Green Bay also added __Javon Hargrave__ (Min) and __Zaire Franklin__ (Ind) in free agency, but it lost far more talent in __Romeo Doubs__ (NE), __Quay Walker__ (LV), and __Rashan Gary__ (Dal), among others. Green Bay’s odds haven’t cratered, but they’re notably lower than they were all of last season until Week 18.

### __Seattle Seahawks__

\>+1000 odds (9.09% implied odds) to +950 odds (9.52%)

The Seahawks are still the second-favorite to win the Super Bowl, but their implied odds to hoist the Lombardi Trophy took a small dip (-.43%) following the draft. Seattle entered the draft with just four selections — they eventually left with eight picks after a pair of trade downs — and there was no chance they were leaving it without using one of those selections on a running back after losing __Kenneth Walker__ to Kansas City in free agency. GM __John Schneider__ admitted after Day 1 that they tried to trade down from No. 32 to collect more picks, but they didn’t want to move far enough down where they wouldn’t have a shot to select Price in the second round. Seattle remains one of the league’s most complete teams after winning the Super Bowl with an average margin of victory of 18.3 points in the postseason, but it has slight concerns in its backfield and secondary.

### __Minnesota Vikings__

\>+5500 odds (1.79% implied odds) to +5000 odds (1.96%)

The Vikings got a bump in their Super Bowl odds from +6000 to +5000 after making one of the bigger splashes in free agency. They signed __Kyler Murray__ to try to complete a roster that reached nine wins despite a miserable QB situation led by the overmatched __J.J. McCarthy__. Minnesota’s odds settled back a bit to +5500 for a -.17% dip in implied odds after reaching for __Caleb Banks__ at No. 18 to replace __Javon Hargrave__ and __Jonathan Allen__. The Vikings also traded __Jonathan Greenard__ to the Eagles during the draft, who had 12+ sacks in back-to-back seasons before a down 2025 campaign. It’s a good time to buy at these slightly longer odds if you like the Vikings this season. Minnesota could sign some veterans at safety, iOL, or WR — [like](https://x.com/AdamSchefter/status/2049175084934340767?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2049175084934340767%7Ctwgr%5E955494025a6dfc6504984c3f128dcb100c037e0c%7Ctwcon%5Es1_c10&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fvikingswire.usatoday.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2Fnfl%2Fvikings%2F2026%2F04%2F29%2Fvikings-host-former-49ers-wr-jauan-jennings-no-deal-reached%2F89855964007%2F) [__Jauan Jennings__](https://x.com/AdamSchefter/status/2049175084934340767?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2049175084934340767%7Ctwgr%5E955494025a6dfc6504984c3f128dcb100c037e0c%7Ctwcon%5Es1_c10&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fvikingswire.usatoday.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2Fnfl%2Fvikings%2F2026%2F04%2F29%2Fvikings-host-former-49ers-wr-jauan-jennings-no-deal-reached%2F89855964007%2F) — thanks to the savings from the Greenard trade.

### __Tennessee Titans__

\>+17500 odds (.57% implied odds) to +15000 odds (.66%)

The Titans surprisingly took a small step back in their implied Super Bowl odds (-.09%) despite drafting a pair of prospects in the first round. Tennessee diverged from mock drafts to select __Carnell Tate__ fourth overall, and he’ll immediately compete to be the #1 WR. It’s promising that the new staff prioritized getting __Cam Ward__ a weapon at the top of the draft after last year’s #1 overall pick gained momentum late in the season. The Titans traded back into the first round to nab a sliding __Keldric Faulk__ at No. 31. He’s coming off just a 2-sack junior season, but he has the traits, size (6’6”, 276 pounds), and explosiveness (35” vertical) to make a leap in __Robert Saleh__’s defense. Tennessee also traded up for Anthony Hill in the late second round to solidify the middle of their defense. The Titans improved during the draft, but their odds drifted because there’s little interest in betting on them to win the Super Bowl.
